newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL shares end lower on foreign fund bearishness.
newsitem.headline: KL shares end lower on foreign fund bearishness.

text.p: Malaysian shares ended lower on Tuesday after foreign institutional funds remained bearish as investors said they found valuations in other regional market cheaper, analysts and dealers said.
At the close the benchmark Composite Index shed 2.76 points, or 0.26 percent, to 1,057.77. The small-capitalised Second Board Index lost 7.20 points, 1.29 percent, to 552.73.

"The selling has been mostly by foreigners. Morgan Stanley has been clearing their positions for some time, but their report published yesterday could have prompted others to also sell," said a dealing manager at a large local brokerage.

U.S. brokerage house Morgan Stanley downgraded Malaysia in a report issued to Reuters on Monday. The investment firm said they were lowering their weighting on Malaysia by one percentage point to seven percent.

Political turmoil in Cambodia was also having a negative effect on regional fund managers as numerous Malaysian companies have investments in the country. However, most of these companies only have a limited exposure to the country, said analysts.
Water utility Puncak Niaga ended its first trading day at 4.48 against a 4.76 opening price and 3.80 offer price.

Hotel and casino operator Resorts World fell 15 cents to 6.95 with 3.0 million shares traded, making it one of the most actively-traded stocks. Analysts said the company is facing stiff competition from casinos and resorts in other parts of the region.
National power utility Tenaga Nasional fell 10 cents to 12.0 ringgit. The stock has around 10 percent weighting on the Composite Index.
Market volume totalled 268 million shares, valued at 1.75 billion ringgit. Losers thumped gainers 515 to 113.
On the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange, the spot July contract rose 1.4 points to 1,050.0 with 753 lots traded. No other contracts were traded.
